title: OKAY BLENDER FOR THE PRICE; A COUPLE NICE FEATURES, ATTRACTIVE
text: OKAY BLENDER FOR THE PRICE; A COUPLE NICE FEATURES, ATTRACTIVE. The first thing I noticed about this blender is that the blending cup seemed very short and it seemed like it wouldn't hold as much as my other blender which hold 5 cups and is taller.  This holds 6 cups and the reason it can hold more without as much height is that the blending cup is bigger around.  The cup is nice thick glass and is one of the better features of the blender.  The blender is attractive, with a silver colored base, but the base doesn't appear to be metal, but more like a pastic coated with silver material.  Seems powerful enough to do most jobs, but probably more of a light duty blender.  The wattage is 550, which seemed like a lot, but in checking other blenders some are in the 700 to 750 watt range and I'm sure they go higher as well.  The gasket is not a separate piece which is a real plus.  I suppose 12 speeds is nice, but how many speeds do you really need?  I don't even use the 8 speeds on my old blender.  Instructions say that to blend hot liquids you need to leave the cover loose and cover it with a towel.  Seems like a hassle when other blenders will handle hot liquids without doing anything special.  When using it with hot food and liquids, you'll now have a dirty towel to wash.  I usually don't read what other reviewers say, as I don't want to be influenced one way or another, but I noticed several who had a problem with the plastic blender cup base breaking easily.  With a two year warranty and the low price of this blender, you probably can't go wrong, but it's not fun to wait for replacement parts.  You also have to search for your receipt and whatever else might be required for warranty service or return.  If I wanted a quality power tool, I wouldn't think twice about selecting Black & Decker as they make good power tools.  Are their small appliances as good?  Probably not.  I recommend buying a blender from a manufacturer who has a long history of making quality blenders.  Apparently Black & Decker acquired General Electric's small appliance division in 1984, so it would seem they have over 20 years of experience, but contrast this with the Waring Blender company that has been making blenders since the 1930's.  There are so many blenders available in the market and there probably isn't a lot of difference amongst them until you start getting up into higher prices.  Seems like there is a lot of competition in the market for blenders and this is a low end competitor is good enough for people who don't use a blender every day.  If you are constantly using your blender (like for a daily smoothie), select something more rugged that costs more.  This is by no means a food processor; I think it is wise to spend more and get a combo food processor and blender, which should serve your needs longer.  This is probably good for a cheap, attractive gift, especially for someone just starting out who really needs a blender.
